Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Prabir Halder, Advocates -------- For the Petitioner in WP No. 1448 of 2008. 
Mahmudul Islam with Md Mizanul Hoq Chowdhury Advocates -------- For the Petitioner in WP No. 3071 of 2008 
Razik-al-Jalil, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Abdus Samad Kamal, Assistant Attorney-General -------- For the Respondents.
parties:
Nasirullah and another -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh and others -------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Because of increase of population and vehicles in Dhaka City Corporation (in short, DCC), the Government imposed restrictions on plying trucks within the city from morning to 8-00/9-00 PM As a result, the members of English Road Iron and Steel Merchants Association (in short, the Association) have been facing serious problems in carrying on their business. The Association through the petitioner had been looking for a piece of land at Jatrabari area of DCC in order to set up godowns for its members with sufficient space for loading and unloading of trucks within the area of their godowns. After extensive search, the petitioner found out the land measuring an area of 1041 acres in that area. A total of 119 members of the Association became interested in purchasing land in their own names but to use that land jointly for the business. The purchase was made as back as in 1988. The members of the Association initially set up godowns for storing commodities in the purchased land and also had been giving delivery 01' bulk sale from there by unloading and loading trucks. They established shops on that land and ultimately, turned it into a market. The market bears a signboard, which reads "English Road Iron and Steel Merchants Association Jatrabari Market". The Association purchased land from RS plot No. 2357 corresponding to Mahanagar survey plot Nos. 4943 and 4945 and those two plots are contiguous to a vast vacant land of Mahan agar Survey plot NoA805. Mahanagar Survey plot Nos. 4951, 4994, 4999, 5000, 5001, 5002 and 5003 are situated by the side of Dhaka-Chittagong highway where a wholesale market for vegetables has been functioning. Plot No. 5003 is contiguous to plot No. 4805. All of a sudden, the petitioner came to know about the service of a notice dated 12-7-2007 under the signature of respondent No.6 on behalf of respondent No. 7 under section 3 of The Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (in short, the Ordinance). The notice was served on Mr A Samad, an owner of the land recorded in RS plot No. 2357. The notice disclosed the intention of the Government for acquisition of 5 acres of land from RS plot No. 2357. The total quantum of the land of RS plot No. 2357 is 11.08 acres. Respondent No. 6 also affixed a notice under section 3 of the Ordinance on the notice board of respondent No.3 mentioning RS plot No. 2357 and two others. After perusal of the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance, the petitioner found that though proposal was made for acquiring land from RS Plot No. 2357, description of the land to be acquired was vague and indefinite for not specifying the boundaries of 5 acres out of 11.08 acres of land of that plot. As soon as the petitioner came to know about the notice, he submitted objection to respondent No. 3 stating details and praying for excluding the land of the Association from the proposal of acquisition as the land was being used for public purpose. As there is no response against the objection from respondent No.3, the petitioner on 9-9-2007 submitted another objection to respondent No. 2. Hearing the objection, respondent No.3 assured the petitioner of consideration of his prayer after obtaining a report from the concerned officers about the existence of the vast vacant area of land of Plot No.4805 adjacent to the land proposed to be acquired. On 14-11-2007, the Association received a notice dated 12-11-2007 under section 6 of the Ordinance from respondent No. 6, on behalf of respondent No. 3, directing the members of the Samity to appear before him and for giving statements about their interest in the property and fixing the next date for 25-11-2007. Respondent No.6 on behalf of respondent No.3 issued another notice dated 5-2-2008 under section 7 of the Ordinance upon each of the members who purchased the land described in the schedule to the Writ Petition. The members of the Association are still in possession of the land in question and have been carrying on business there. Since the petitioner failed to impress upon the concerned authority to release the disputed land from acquisition, he filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained this Rule Nisi. 

 The petitioner purchased .64 acre of land of mouza Jatrabari, PS Demra from the successor-in- interest of RS recorded owner Mr Alauddin by the registered deed of sale dated 6-3-2000. The purchased land appertains to CS plot No. 597 under CS Khatian No.118, SA plot No.597, under SA khatian No.294 and RS plot No.2357 under RS Khatian No. 57. The petitioner got his name mutated both in the RS and SA khatians. While the petitioner was in possession of the land in question, the officials of DCC came to evict him on 3-4-2008 stating that the land was acquired by respondent No. 1 for the purpose of development of Jatrabari Wholesale Kachcha Bazar of DCC. The petitioner was taken aback as no notice was served upon him under sections 3, 5, 6 and 7 of the Ordinance. The petitioner filed an application to the Mayor, DCC for releasing his 0.64 acre of land from acquisition proposal. In reply to the application, the DCC stated that the land in question was acquired by respondent No.1 after complying with the provisions of law as evidenced by Annexure-C 1 dated 10-4-2008. On query, the petitioner came to know that notices under sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Ordinance were not issued/served upon the petitioner in LA Case No. 1 of 2007-2008. Without executing any agreement according to section 15(1) of the Ordinance, the LA case was started. Notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance were not served upon the petitioner though his name was duly mutated in RS khatian No.57, vide Mutation Nothi No. 11205 of 2004 and Mutation Khatian No. 1716. The existing Kacha Bazar has been developed almost wholly on the khas land earlier used by DCC as garbage dumping station. Of total 11.08 acres of land of RS plot No. 2357, an area measuring 6.30 acres is the khas land of the Government. On 3-4-2008, the officials of DCC went to the location and demarcated the area by hoisting red flags at four points covering partial Kachcha Bazar and partial Iron and Steel Market. Only 5.0102 acres of land have been proposed for acquisition for the development of Kacha Bazar but no specific demarcation of the proposed land was mentioned in the notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance. The petitioner collected a notice which revealed that the Assistant Commissioner (Land) took step for recovery of the khas land measuring 6.30 acres of RS plot No.2357. Respondent No. 9 issued a letter to the Deputy Commissioner by memo dated 25-5-1998 informing the decision of the National Economic Committee regarding (1) the use of Government khas land in implementing the development project and directing the Deputy Commissioner to use khas land first, failing which, they can acquire land, (2) video recording of the location of the proposed project. As per provisions of section 15(1) of the Ordinance, an agreement between the acquiring authority and the requiring body is mandatory before issuance of notice under section 3 in respect of the property proposed to be acquired for any person other than the Government. Failing to impress upon the concerned authority to release the land from acquisition, the petitioner obtained this Rule Nisi from this Court on 20-4-2008. 

 (4) ভূমি প্রশাসন ম্যানুয়েল 2nd part provides that the land used for carrying on business should be kept outside the purview of acquisition when khas land is available. The proposal for acquiring land belonging to private individuals should be avoided. In the instant case, RS plot No. 2357 corresponding to Mohanagar Survey plot Nos. 4943 and 4945 measuring more than 11.08 acres belonging to the Government has been lying vacant and the proposed market can be established there. 

 (5) No agreement was entered into between the Government and Dee under section 3( 1) of the Ordinance and, as such, the very acquisition is illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 7. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 in addition to the grounds agitated by Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, submits that no notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance was served upon the petitioner and, as such, the proceeding of the impugned  LA Case so far as the petitioner concerned is illegal and without jurisdiction. He further submits that as per the map prepared by the acquiring authority, the land owned by the petitioner does not fall within it. He lastly submits that video recording was not made as per the Acquisition of Immovable Property Rules, 1982 (in short, the Rules). 

 8. The learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of respondent No. 3, on the other hand, submits that the acquisition in question was made after observing all legal formalities and, as such, there is nothing to interfere with acquisition proceeding. He further submits that meanwhile, Gazette notification had been published and, as such, the property vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. He then submits that the video recording of land proposed to be acquired was made 5 days after issuance of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance and that the video recording shows that all existing structures were intact and that the petitioner did not raise any objection as to demolition of any structure by the requiring body prior to video recording. He also submits that notice was served upon the vender of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 in accordance with law. He then submits that no agreement is required to be entered into between the Government and the DCC which is merely executing the decision of the Government for establishing four wholesale green vegetable markets in Dhaka City. In elaborating his submission, he states that DCC is under the Ministry of Local Government and DCC being a governmental organisation, no such agreement is required. He however, submits that later, Dee entered into an agreement with the Government and even if there is any defect, that was cured later. 

 "6( 1) When the Government, the Divisional Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner, as the case may be, has made a decision for acquisition of any property under section 5 or the proviso to section 4(3)(b), as the case may be, the Deputy Commissioner shall cause public notice to be given in the prescribed manner at convenient places on or near such property stating that the Government, the Divisional Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner, as the case may be, has decided to acquire the property and intends to take possession thereof and that claims for compensation for all with interests in such property may be made to him. 

 (2) Such notice shall state the particulars of the property to, be acquired and taken possession of, and shall require all persons interested in the property to appear personally or by agent before the Deputy Commissioner at a time, not being earlier than fifteen days after date of publication of the notice, and place mentioned therein and to state the nature of their respective interest in the property and the amount and particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests. 

 16. In this regard, reliance may be placed on the case of Abdur Rouf Chowdhury vs Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land and Acquisition) 3 BLC 330 in which it is held that although the petitioners were interested in the property under acquisition, no notice was served upon them under section 6(3) of the Ordinance. This irregularity in the procedure will not ipso facto render the acquisition illegal provided that acquisition was for a public purpose and compensation amount was adequate and fixed in accordance with law. 

 The notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance show that there is no specification of what quantum of land was being acquired from each of the plots proposed to be acquired. Before initiation of the acquisition process, the requiring body made a survey of the land proposed to be acquired and also its adjoining area. The map reveals that prior to issuing notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance, the land proposed to be acquired was clearly identified in map dated 21-5-2007 which was produced before the Court at the hearing of the Rule Nisi. 

 "After having heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner the learned Judge of the High Court Division said that no such question (vagueness) was raised before the acquisition authority and accordingly, found no substance in the contention." 

 20. It is contended on behalf of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 that an area of land measuring 6.30 acres appertaining to RS plot No. 2357 is the khas land. The petitioner stated that the Assistant Commissioner (Land) issued a notice (Annexure-F) to the General Hospital (Private Limited) for recovery of khas land measuring 6.30 acres appertaining to RS plot No. 2357. The CS record shows that the land claimed to be the khas land belonged to a private individual. The SA khatian in respect of that land was, however, prepared in the name of the Government. The basis of preparation of SA khatian in the name of the Government could not be satisfactorily established by either party. In such a state of affairs, it cannot be conclusively said at this stage that the khas land standing in the name of the Government in RS khatian belongs to the Government. Annexure-F of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 shows that a private hospital is on a portion of that khas land. Since setting up of a vegetable market is very urgent, taking over possession of land belonging to the Government in occupation of somebody else may take time. Therefore, the contention that the wholesale green vegetable market can be set up on the khas land does not stand to reason. 

 "Reading all the sections together, sections 8, 9, 10, 12 and 15, it is clear that abatement will take place if the acquiring authority fails to "pay" or "deposit" compensation in terms of section 10 within one year from the date of decision of the Government (which is section 5 in the case of acquisition). The requiring body, therefore, will deposit the consideration money with the Government well ahead of expiry of one year from the date of decision of the Government but within what date, is a subject matter of agreement between the Government and the requiring body under section IS. This is their internal arrangement, but legal consequence of abatement will follow only when the Government fails to 'pay' or 'deposit' compensation it terms of section 10." 

 28. The above condition was appended while the Committee accorded approval to the acquisition of the land in question. Therefore, DCC is under the obligation to abide by the decision of the Central Land Allocation Committee, Consequently, as soon as the constructions of the wholesale green vegetable markets are completed, the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008 and the affected shop owners having admitted title to the acquired land will get first priority in the allotment of shops. DCC cannot deviate from the direction of the Central Land Allocation Committee. 

 29. Mr Prabir Halder, learned Advocate for the petitioners of Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008, submits that notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was not issued by a competent person and, as such, all actions taken in respect of acquisition of the land in question will fall through. 

 30. Admittedly, notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was issued under the signature of Mr Ishaque Mia, Additional Land Acquisition Officer and authorised officer on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 12-7-2007. It is, of course, true that Mr Md Ishaque Mia was under order of transfer when he issued the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance and he was succeeded by Mr Bibakananda Sarker who joined the Land Acquisition Section, Dhaka on 9-7 -2007 as evidenced by Annexure-11 to the affidavit-in-opposition filed in Writ Petition No. 1448 of 2008. The learned Deputy Attorney- General submits that there are as many as nine branches in Land Acquisition Section, each branch is manned by an Additional Land Acquisition Officer. Amplifying his submission, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, submits that Mr Bibak- ananda Sarker joined in the LA section of Dhaka on 9-7-2007 but did not take charge of the 9th Branch of LA Section. Annexure-12 of the affidavit-in- opposition indicates that Mr Md Ishaque Mia made over charge of the 9th branch of the LA Section to Mr Bibakananda Sarker on 19-7-2007. Therefore, it is crystal clear that prior to 19-7-2007, Mr  Md Ishaque Mia was competent to issue notice under section 3 of the Ordinance. As a result, the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner does not hold good. 

 31. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate for the petitioner of Writ Petitioner No. 3071 of 2008, contends that the video recording of the land proposed to be acquired was not done according to the Acquisition of the Immovable Property Rules, 1982 (in short, the Rules) and, as such, the entire acquisition proceeding is illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 33. From the above Rule, it appears that the use of the word "immediately" prior to the words "before publishing notice under section 3 of the Ordinance" is very significant. Having considered the entire Rule, in general, we are of the opinion that video recording has to be done immediately before issuance of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance but not before taking decision of acquisition of the land. Therefore, in the decision-making process of acquisition, this Rule had no role to play. The petitioners are aggrieved by the decision of acquisition, not by the delay in video recording of the land. 

 35. Therefore, we are of the view that a delay of five days in video recording of the land is not fatal to render the entire acquisition proceeding illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 36. It is contended on behalf of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of2008 that the land of the petitioner does not fall within the land under acquisition and therefore, notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance was illegally issued in respect of the land of the petitioner. 

 Whether or not the land of the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 3071 of 2008 falls within the acquisition is a disputed question of fact and such question cannot be resolved without measurement and taking evidence which is beyond the purview of the writ jurisdiction. 

 38. In the light of the findings made before, we do not like to interfere with the acquisition process.
